learning: Hypotheses: (1) Finer spacing sharpens the centre-line signal on bends, lowering s-bend and slalom max_error. (2) Oval steering_oscillation stays below 0.25 (iteration 7 was 0.208). (3) If s-bend and slalom progress stay near 0.14 and 0.19 with max_error unchanged, the plateau is turn response or controller-side, so the next lever is wheel_track or controller gains. Report per-track progress, max_error, steering_oscillation and oval finish rate.
notes: Iteration 10 tests the Builder's 7-sensor array (0.0267 m spacing, span x = -0.08 to 0.08, y 0.05 m), with only the sensor count and spacing changed from the iteration-7 best. Weights are scaled x/0.04 to keep the iteration-7 sensitivity. Revert to five sensors if the score drops below about 300.
rationale: Iteration 7 (5 sensors, 0.04 m spacing, mass 0.5 kg, track 0.10 m, body 0.10 x 0.12 m) is still the best raced design at 315.27. Its oval finish is 75%, and its s-bend and slalom max_error is stuck at about 0.062 to 0.064 with zero or near-zero line loss, so the limit is centre-line resolution or turn response, not line loss. Iteration 8 showed that sensor y 0.03 m is clearly worse, so y stays at 0.05 m. I adopt the Builder's 7-sensor test: x = -0.08 to 0.08 at about 0.0267 m spacing, y 0.05 m, footprint 0.016 m, and every other geometry field unchanged. The controller weights scale as x/0.04, giving [-2, -1.333, -0.667, 0, 0.667, 1.333, 2], which keeps the iteration-7 signal sensitivity per metre. kp 6, ki 0.05, kd 0.9, base_speed 1.5 and last_direction are unchanged, so the race isolates array density. Expected result: s-bend and slalom max_error below 0.062 with progress above about 0.19, and oval finish at or above 65%. Risk: extra sensors could add noise and raise oval oscillation. If the score falls below about 300 or the oval finish falls below 65%, revert to the five-sensor iteration-7 geometry.
